blocks.source: 12. The one-loop equivariant structure from the quantum master equation

Chapters 9–11 computed the one-loop components of local operators from two-body kernels, and several inputs of that computation were identities read off the structure of the regulator: the dilatation component as four times the logarithmic coefficient, the coefficient $\theta=-\tfrac13$ from the arity-two component of $L\circ L=0$, the special supercharges from the supercharges by the position decomposition, $K=P^\dagger$, and the comparison with the holomorphic twist.

This chapter derives every one-loop component from the equivariant quantum master equation at scale $\varepsilon$: the obstruction of Definition 8.7 along each generator is computed from the graphs with one special edge, the equation $s(\hbar F_1)=\hbar\,\mathrm{Ob}$ is solved arity by arity with all its free directions, and the components on local operators follow from the defect flow of Lemma 8.4 through the local representative of Definition 8.14.

The construction needs new input at three places: along the supercharges the composite line has a nonzero image under $Q$, so the obstruction is a finite sum of regulator graphs computed graph by graph; the free directions of the arity-one solution are fixed by the arity-two equations, which therefore carry the coefficient $\theta$; and the finite counterterm vertices of Chapters 10 and 11 cancel against the bridges, so that the two-body kernels are the finite parts of the defect cycles themselves.
The former shortcuts become theorems of the construction or cross-checks, and every component is stated as a representative together with its class, the part that is independent of the scheme.

The unit is $\frac{\hbar\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)}{16\pi^2(X,Y)}$, equal to $-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}$ for $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{su}(N)$ (Remark 6.13), and a number followed by “units” is that number times the unit.

Edges carry $P(\varepsilon,T)$ of Definition 8.3; the special edge is $K_\varepsilon-K_0=-\int_0^\varepsilon(H\otimes1)K_t\,dt$, the factor $e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}-1$ times the components of $K_0$ (Proposition 4.27).

The endpoint $T$ is the endpoint of the transfer of [C07]; every component below is independent of it (Theorem 8.15 (ii)), and it is taken as $T=\infty$ where the graph sums converge at generic momenta (Proposition 8.25) and finite along $K_b$ and along the pairs $(K_b,P_{b'})$ and $(\eta,\eta')$ with $\Gamma(\eta,\eta')|_V\neq0$ (Definition 8.26).
The bracket is that of Definition 1.6, and $s=d_{CE}+\{S_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)},-\}$ on cochains (Theorem 8.8).

We write $\mathcal N:=2\int(A,A^*)-4\int(\lambda^*,\lambda)-\int(c^*,c)$ for the field-counting functional of Chapter 6, whose bracket multiplies the coordinate functionals of $c$, $A$, $\lambda$, $A^*$, $\lambda^*$, $c^*$ by $1$, $2$, $4$, $-2$, $-4$, $-1$ (Lemma 6.7).

Every number of this chapter is computed by the two independent evaluations of Remark 12.69, unless a statement says otherwise; the two-component forms of Definition 8.1 of the main formulas are collected in Remark 12.72.
12.1 The component equations of the quantum master equation
Definition 12.1 (Generators, their data and the sector parts).

The functional $S^{(1)}(x)$ of Definition 2.12 has degree $-1$ and Weyl weight $4-\tfrac12\lambda_x$, the position counted at weight $-1$.

The index $d$ of a sector runs over $\{\perp,\lambda,V\}$ for even $x$ and over $\{V,\perp\}$ for odd $x$.

The quadratic part of a solution $\hbar F_1^{(1)}(x)$ contains $\sum_d\theta^x_d$ units times the sector parts; $\theta^\Delta_\perp$, $\theta^\Delta_\lambda$, $\theta^\Delta_V$ are $\theta$, $\theta_\lambda$, $\theta_V$ of Definition 11.19 and $\theta^{P_b}_d$ are $\theta_P$, $\theta_{P,\lambda}$, $\theta_{P,V}$.
When the $\theta^x_d$ are equal, their common value $t_x$ is the uniform coefficient: the coefficient, in units, of $S^{(1)}(x)$ with its cubic part.
Definition 12.2 (Components of cochains, of the obstruction and of the logarithmic coefficient).

A local cochain $f$ of $C^\bullet(\mathfrak{psl}(4|4),\mathscr O_l(\mathscr E))$ has components $f^{(k)}(x_1,\dots,x_k)$ (Definition 2.7), normalised as in Lemma 2.11: the arity-one component of $d_{CE}f+\tfrac12\{f,f\}$ at $f=S_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}$ is $\{S,S^{(1)}(x)\}$, and its arity-two component is $\{S,S^{(2)}(x,y)\}+S^{(1)}([x,y])+(-1)^{|x|}\{S^{(1)}(x),S^{(1)}(y)\}$.
$\mathrm{Ob}^{(k)}$ and $\hbar F_1^{(k)}$ are the components of the one-loop obstruction of Definition 8.7 and of the finite counterterm $\hbar F_1$ of Definition 8.5 in this normalisation.

We write $I^{CT,(k)}$ for the components of the counterterm cochain $I^{CT}_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}[\varepsilon]$, and $L$ for its coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$, with components $L^{(0)}$, $L^{(1)}(x)$, $L^{(2)}(x,y)$; $L^{(0)}$ is the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ in $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ and $L^{(1)}(x)$ that in $I^{CT}_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}[\varepsilon]^{(1)}(x)$, as in Theorem 11.40 (iv).
Lemma 12.3 (The derivation rule of the bracket).
Let $\{f,g\}_{\rm std}$ be the odd bracket with $\Delta_0(fg)=\Delta_0(f)g+(-1)^{|f|}f\Delta_0(g)+(-1)^{|f|}\{f,g\}_{\rm std}$.

Then the bracket of Definition 1.6 is $\{f,g\}=(-1)^{|f|}\{f,g\}_{\rm std}$, and every derivation $\mathcal D$ of degree $1$ of $\{,\}_{\rm std}$, in particular $Q$, $\{I,-\}$, $Q+\{I,-\}$ and $\{F,-\}$ for $F$ of degree $0$, satisfies
\mathcal D\{a,b\}=-\{\mathcal Da,b\}-(-1)^{|a|}\{a,\mathcal Db\}. \tag{12.1}
Proof.
Definition 1.6 gives $\{f,g\}=\Delta_0(fg)-\Delta_0(f)g-(-1)^{|f|}f\Delta_0(g)$, which is $(-1)^{|f|}\{f,g\}_{\rm std}$.
A derivation of degree $1$ satisfies $\mathcal D\{a,b\}_{\rm std}=\{\mathcal Da,b\}_{\rm std}+(-1)^{|a|+1}\{a,\mathcal Db\}_{\rm std}$; multiplying by $(-1)^{|a|}$ and using $|\mathcal Da|=|a|+1$,
\mathcal D\{a,b\}=(-1)^{|a|}(-1)^{|a|+1}\{\mathcal Da,b\}-\{a,\mathcal Db\}_{\rm std}=-\{\mathcal Da,b\}-(-1)^{|a|}\{a,\mathcal Db\}.
Lemma 12.4 (Components of the defect vertex of the action).

Let $J=I_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}-I^{CT}_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}[\varepsilon]-\hbar F_1$ and let $\mathfrak d:=(d_{CE}+Q)J+\tfrac12\{J,J\}_\varepsilon+\hbar\Delta_\varepsilon J$ be the defect vertex of Lemma 8.4.
Write $\{f,g\}_\varepsilon=\{f,g\}+\{f,g\}^\sigma_\varepsilon$, the second term being minus $f$ and $g$ joined by one special edge, and $I^{CT}:=I^{CT}_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}[\varepsilon]$.
Modulo $\hbar^2$ and constants,

\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak d^{(0)}={}&\tfrac12\{I,I\}^\sigma_\varepsilon-Q\,I^{CT,(0)}-\{I,I^{CT,(0)}\}_\varepsilon-\hbar\big(QF_1^{(0)}+\{I,F_1^{(0)}\}_\varepsilon\big),\\
\mathfrak d^{(1)}(x)={}&\{I,S^{(1)}(x)\}^\sigma_\varepsilon+\hbar\Delta_\varepsilon S^{(1)}(x)-Q\,I^{CT,(1)}(x)-\{I,I^{CT,(1)}(x)\}_\varepsilon-\{I^{CT,(0)},S^{(1)}(x)\}_\varepsilon\\
&-\hbar\big(QF_1^{(1)}(x)+\{I,F_1^{(1)}(x)\}_\varepsilon+\{F_1^{(0)},S^{(1)}(x)\}_\varepsilon\big),\\
\mathfrak d^{(2)}(x,y)={}&(-1)^{|x|}\{S^{(1)}(x),S^{(1)}(y)\}^\sigma_\varepsilon+\{I,S^{(2)}(x,y)\}^\sigma_\varepsilon-\Big[Q\,I^{CT,(2)}(x,y)+\{I,I^{CT,(2)}(x,y)\}_\varepsilon+I^{CT,(1)}([x,y])\\
&+(-1)^{|x|}\big(\{I^{CT,(1)}(x),S^{(1)}(y)\}_\varepsilon+\{S^{(1)}(x),I^{CT,(1)}(y)\}_\varepsilon\big)+\{I^{CT,(0)},S^{(2)}(x,y)\}_\varepsilon\Big]-\hbar\big[\text{the same with }F_1\text{ in place of }I^{CT}\big],
\end{aligned} \tag{12.2}
with $\hbar\Delta_\varepsilon I=0$, $\hbar\Delta_\varepsilon S^{(1)}(x)$ a constant for even $x$ and $0$ for odd $x$, and $\hbar\Delta_\varepsilon S^{(2)}(x,y)=0$.
Proof.

The part of order $\hbar^0$ without special edge is $d_{CE}I_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}+\tfrac12\{I_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)},I_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}\}$, which vanishes by (2.4); its arity components are those of Lemma 2.11, and the remainder is the special-edge part of each bracket.
The terms linear in $I^{CT}$ and in $F_1$ are the linearisation of the same component formulas at $S_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}$ (Lemma 12.6 (i)), with the bracket at scale $\varepsilon$.

$\Delta_\varepsilon$ contracts a field with its own antifield inside one monomial: in $I$ it gives $\operatorname{tr}\mathrm{ad}=0$ (proof of Theorem 4.30); in $S^{(1)}(x)$ for even $x$ the terms $(v.e,e^*)$ give the field-independent supertrace of $v.\,e^{-\varepsilon H}$; the quadratic terms of $S^{(1)}(\xi)$ and $S^{(1)}(\eta)$ pair $\lambda$ with $A^*$ and $A$ with $\lambda^*$, the cubic terms have the legs $A$, $A$, $\lambda^*$, and $s_0$ the legs $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda^*$; the terms of $S^{(2)}$ in (2.8) have the legs $(\lambda^*,\lambda^*)$ and $(A,c^*)$.
Definition 12.5 (Arity components of the obstruction and residuals).

With $F_1=0$, $\mathrm{Ob}$ is the local cochain of degree $1$ of Definition 8.7: its tree-level flow with edges $P(0,T)$ is the coefficient of $\hbar$ of the $\varepsilon\to0$ limit of the connected graphs with one vertex $\mathfrak d$, the other vertices from $J$ and edges $P(\varepsilon,T)$.
In the normalisation of Definition 12.2 the equation $s(\hbar F_1)=\hbar\,\mathrm{Ob}$ of Theorem 8.8 (ii) reads, arity by arity,

Given a solution of the first equation, the arity-one residual is $\mathcal R^{(1)}(x):=\hbar\,\mathrm{Ob}^{(1)}(x)-\{\hbar F_1^{(0)},S^{(1)}(x)\}$; given also a solution of the second, the arity-two residual $\mathcal R^{(2)}(x,y)$ is $\hbar\,\mathrm{Ob}^{(2)}(x,y)$ minus the terms of the third equation that contain $F_1^{(1)}$ and $F_1^{(0)}$.

$\mathrm{Ob}^{(1)}(x)$ is local of degree $0$ and Weyl weight $4-\tfrac12\lambda_x$, $\mathrm{Ob}^{(2)}(x,y)$ of degree $-1$ and weight $4-\tfrac12(\lambda_x+\lambda_y)$, and $\hbar F_1^{(1)}(x)$, $\hbar F_1^{(2)}(x,y)$ have degrees $-1$, $-2$ and the same weights.
The arity-one equation with $\hbar F_1^{(0)}$ in the form of (11.9) is the second equation, $\{\hbar F_1^{(0)},S^{(1)}(x)\}=\{S^{(1)}(x),\hbar F_1^{(0)}\}$ for $F_1^{(0)}$ even of degree $0$.
Lemma 12.6 (Component formulas of $s$ and the Wess–Zumino identities).

• (i) For a cochain $F$ of degree $0$, $(sF)^{(0)}=(Q+\{I,-\})F^{(0)}$, $(sF)^{(1)}(x)=(Q+\{I,-\})F^{(1)}(x)+\{F^{(0)},S^{(1)}(x)\}$, and $(sF)^{(2)}(x,y)$ is the left side of the third equation of [(12.3)](#c12-02875) with $F$ in place of $\hbar F_1$.
• (iii) (Wess–Zumino.)
Since $s\,\mathrm{Ob}=0$ (Theorem 8.8 (i)),
and the residuals are closed: $(Q+\{I,-\})\mathcal R^{(1)}(x)=0$ when the arity-zero equation holds, and $(Q+\{I,-\})\mathcal R^{(2)}(x,y)=0$ when the equations of arity zero and one hold.
Proof.
(i) Differentiate the component formulas of Lemma 2.11 along $S_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}+tF$, with $\tfrac d{dt}\tfrac12\{f,f\}=\{f,\dot f\}$ for even $f$.

(ii) The components of $sG$ are universal expressions $(Q+\{I,-\})G^{(2)}+\alpha\,G^{(1)}([x,y])+\beta\{G^{(1)}(x),S^{(1)}(y)\}+\gamma\{S^{(1)}(x),G^{(1)}(y)\}+\delta\{G^{(0)},S^{(2)}(x,y)\}$ and $(Q+\{I,-\})G^{(1)}(x)+\delta_1\{G^{(0)},S^{(1)}(x)\}$, and $s^2=0$ fixes the coefficients on the exact cochains $G=sF$, with the derivation rule (12.1) and $(Q+\{I,-\})S^{(1)}(x)=0$.
so $\alpha=\gamma=-1$ and $\beta=(-1)^{|x|}$.

For $F=F^{(0)}$ at arity two, $(Q+\{I,-\})S^{(2)}(x,y)=-S^{(1)}([x,y])-(-1)^{|x|}\{S^{(1)}(x),S^{(1)}(y)\}$ (Lemma 2.11) and the derivation rule for $\{F^{(0)},-\}$ cancel every term except $(\delta-1)\{(Q+\{I,-\})F^{(0)},S^{(2)}(x,y)\}$, so $\delta=1$.
(iii) Insert $G=\mathrm{Ob}$ and $G=\hbar\,\mathrm{Ob}-s(\hbar F_1)$, whose lower components vanish.
Proposition 12.7 (Pole structure of the counterterm cochain).
At one loop
I^{CT}_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}[\varepsilon]=\tfrac94\,\varepsilon^{-1}\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(A,A)\ \text{units}+\log\varepsilon\cdot L, \tag{12.5}
with $L$ a local cochain of degree $0$: the components of arity one and two have no pole.
Proof.

The coefficient of $\varepsilon^{-m}$ of $I^{CT,(k)}(x_1,\dots,x_k)$ is a colour-singlet local functional of degree $-k$, total Weyl weight $4-\tfrac12\sum_i\lambda_{x_i}-2m$ and position degree at most $\sum_ip_{x_i}$ (Proposition 10.47).

A colour singlet of degree $-1$ has an antifield and a second adjoint field, field weight at least $4$, or $\tfrac72$ with the legs $(A,\lambda^*)$ when the generator supplies a spinor; one of degree $-2$ has field weight at least $5$, or $\tfrac{11}2$ with an odd number of spinor legs.
The total weight is at least the field weight minus the position degree, and for $m\ge1$ the inequality fails in every case:
In arity zero the weight $4-2m$ with $m\ge1$ leaves the legs $(A,A)$ at weight $2$, the term of Theorem 4.16.
One loop gives integer powers of $\varepsilon$ and the first power of $\log\varepsilon$ (Lemma 4.6).
Proposition 12.8 (The logarithmic coefficient is $s$-closed).
In components, $(Q+\{I,-\})L^{(0)}=0$, $(Q+\{I,-\})L^{(1)}(x)+\{L^{(0)},S^{(1)}(x)\}=0$, and the arity-two formula of Lemma 12.6 (i) applied to $L$ vanishes.
With $L^{(0)}=(Q+\{I,-\})\mathcal N$ units (Theorem 4.22),
L^{(1)}(x)-\big\{\mathcal N,S^{(1)}(x)\big\}\ \text{units} \tag{12.6}
is $(Q+\{I,-\})$-closed of degree $-1$.
Proof.

By [C07, Thm B] and Definition 8.5 the flow $W(P(\varepsilon,T),I_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}-I^{CT})$ has a limit; $Q$ acts on plane-wave values by polynomial substitutions, so the flow of $\mathfrak d$ has a limit (Lemma 8.4).

In this flow at order $\hbar$ the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ comes from the trees of the counterterm vertices of (12.2): their parts without special edge give $-\log\varepsilon\,(sL)$, their special-edge parts carry $(e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}-1)\log\varepsilon\to0$; the cycles with a special edge have no $\log\varepsilon$ (Lemma 12.10), and the subgraphs of the reducible graphs are of these two kinds.
The tree-level flow is injective on local cochains (Theorem 8.15 (i)), so $sL=0$.

Lemma 12.10 (Special-edge lemma).

Let $\mathcal C$ be a cycle all of whose vertices lie on it, with external legs at generic momenta, $n_t$ edges, one special edge $e_\sigma$ and the other edges $P(\varepsilon,T)$, possibly one composite line, with vertices from $I$ and from $S^{(1)}(x)$ and $S^{(1)}(y)$ or $S^{(2)}(x,y)$; along $\eta$, $\Delta$, $M_\omega$ and $K_b$ the position factors at the vertex $S^{(1)}(x)$ are realised by derivatives in a momentum $r$ injected there, at $r=0$.
Let $D$ be its superficial degree and $F_m$ the $m$-th simplex integrand of Definition 10.21.
At $T=\infty$

\mathcal C(\varepsilon)=\sum_{m\ge1}\varepsilon^{-m}a_m+a_0+o(1),\qquad 16\pi^2a_m=\frac1m\int_{\alpha_\sigma\ \text{smallest}}\Big[\big(\min_{f\ne\sigma}\alpha_f\big)^m-\alpha_\sigma^m\Big]F_m\,d\alpha,\qquad 16\pi^2a_0=\int_{\alpha_\sigma\ \text{smallest}}F_0\log\frac{\min_{f\ne\sigma}\alpha_f}{\alpha_\sigma}\,d\alpha, \tag{12.7}
with no term in $\log\varepsilon$; $a_m$ is a polynomial of degree $D-2m$ in the external momenta and in $r$, and $a_0$ a polynomial of degree $D$, zero for $D<0$.
At finite $T$ the coefficients are the same and $T\partial_T\mathcal C(\varepsilon)=O(\varepsilon)$ at fixed $T$.
Proof.

As in Theorems 11.11 and 11.41: the Schwinger domain $\{t_\sigma\le\varepsilon\le t_f\}$ is the difference of the domains with the cutoff shapes $1/\min_{f\ne\sigma}\alpha_f$ and $1/\min_f\alpha_f$, which differ on the region where $\alpha_\sigma$ is the smallest coordinate.
Proposition 10.23 applies to each; the coefficients of $\log\varepsilon$ cancel and the finite parts differ by the stated integral.

The region of large total Schwinger time converges at $T=\infty$ because the external momenta are generic and a composite line is of order $|p|^{-3}$ (Proposition 9.18 (iv)); the injected momentum enters polynomially.

At finite $T$, $T\partial_T$ replaces one edge by $(Q^{GF}\otimes1)K_T$, which confines the loop momentum to $|l|^2\lesssim T^{-1}$, where the special edge is $O(\varepsilon|l|^2)$; the position factors grow at most as $T^{p_x/2}$ and are compensated by the decay of the other edges (Theorem 8.27).
Theorem 12.11 (Graph classes and the local formula for the arity-one obstruction).
Fix a generator $x$ and $n\ge2$.

At order $\hbar$, with $F_1=0$, the part with $n$ legs of the arity-one component along $x$ of the flow of $\mathfrak d$ is the sum of the following classes of connected graphs with edges $P(\varepsilon,T)$, one vertex from (12.2) and one vertex carrying $x$:

• (C) irreducible defect cycles: every vertex on the cycle, exactly one special edge, exactly one vertex $S^{(1)}(x)$ in a placement of Table [12.2](#c12-02905), the other vertices cubic or quartic vertices of $I$ with their external legs; the special edge joins $S^{(1)}(x)$ to $I$ (placement at the special edge) or two vertices of $I$ (line and cubic placements);
• (Rd) reducible graphs: a subgraph of type (C) with fewer legs, or a one-loop subgraph of the arity-zero defect, joined by edges $P(\varepsilon,T)$ to trees of vertices of $I$ and $S^{(1)}(x)$;
• (Br) graphs whose special edge is a bridge;
• (Ct) trees with one counterterm vertex of [(12.2)](#c12-02869) of order $\hbar$, with the parts without and with special edge of each bracket;
• (K) the constant $\hbar\Delta_\varepsilon S^{(1)}(x)$.

As $\varepsilon\to0$, (Br) with the special-edge parts of (Ct) tends to $0$; (Rd) tends to the trees of the components of $\mathrm{Ob}$ with fewer legs; the $\log\varepsilon$ terms of (Ct) cancel identically (Proposition [12.8](#c12-02896)) and (C) has none; the poles satisfy
\sum_{\mathcal C\in(C),\,n=2}a_1(\mathcal C)=\tfrac94\Big\{\int(A,A),S^{(1)}(x)\Big\}\ \text{units},\qquad \sum_{\mathcal C\in(C),\,n}a_m(\mathcal C)=0\quad(m\ge2\ \text{or}\ n\ge3), \tag{12.8}
and
\hbar\,\mathrm{Ob}^{(1)}(x)\big|_{n\ \text{legs}}=\sum_{\mathcal C\in(C),\,n\ \text{legs}}a_0(\mathcal C), \tag{12.9}
a local functional independent of $T$.
With an arity-zero finite counterterm included the same graphs give $\mathcal R^{(1)}(x)$.
Proof.
At order $\hbar$ a connected graph has one cycle and vertices of order $\hbar^0$, or no cycle and one vertex of order $\hbar$ (Proposition 3.22); arity one places $x$ on one vertex.

The marked vertices of order $\hbar^0$ in $\mathfrak d^{(1)}(x)$ and $\mathfrak d^{(0)}$ are special-edge parts, so the special edge lies on the cycle, on a bridge, or on a tree attached to the cycle, which again makes it a bridge.
A graph with the special edge on the cycle is the cycle with trees attached; if a tree is attached through an edge the graph is reducible, otherwise it is in (C).

(Br): removing the bridge separates a one-loop subgraph at a generic momentum $p$; with the counterterm trees of the subgraph and the special-edge part of the counterterm bracket across the same edge, the edge carries $e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}-1$ times the renormalised subgraph, which has a limit (Definition 8.5), so the sum tends to $0$; along $\eta$ and $K_b$ the derivatives in the injected momentum act on $e^{-\varepsilon|p+r|^2}-1$ and on a function of class $C^2$ at $p\neq0$.

(Rd): the subgraph equals the corresponding component of the obstruction plus $o(1)$ after its counterterm trees are included (induction on the number of legs; the arity-zero two-leg subgraphs are Theorem 4.30).

(Ct): by Proposition 12.7 the only pole is $-\varepsilon^{-1}\tfrac94\{\int(A,A),S^{(1)}(x)\}$ units in $-\{I^{CT,(0)},S^{(1)}(x)\}_\varepsilon$, which has two legs, $\{\int(A,A),T_5\}=0$ since $T_5$ has no leg $A^*$.
The flow has a limit (proof of Proposition 12.8), so the poles of (C) cancel this term, which is (12.8), and Lemma 12.10 gives the finite parts.

The tree-level flow of the arity-one part of $\mathrm{Ob}$ with $n$ legs is $\mathrm{Ob}^{(1)}(x)|_n$ plus trees of the components with fewer legs, the limits of (Rd); this gives (12.9), and $T$-independence is Definition 8.7 with Lemma 12.10.
Proposition 12.12 (Composite lines and the commutators with the regulator).

Let $x.$ be the operator of Lemma 11.38 ($v.$ of Definition 7.4 for even $x$), $P\star=Q^{GF}g(H)$, $g(H)=\int_\varepsilon^Te^{-tH}dt$ and $E(H)=e^{-\varepsilon H}-e^{-TH}$, so that $QP\star+P\star Q=E(H)$.
